notes: Awaiting native23 installed final-package direct review. Native21 rejected review is preserved separately.

Final package F front/back: coat, waistcoat, hat and footwear remain assembled without visible rest-pose intersections. Angular candidate surfaces and untextured construction hands are retained limitations.
Final CW/PW front rest views: layered clothing, independent hats/gloves/footwear and silhouette are coherent; no exposed construction anatomy through coat surfaces.

CS raised-arm melee and guard-landing views: gloves, exposed forearms, sleeves, trousers and low shoes follow the registered pose. Angular shoulder folds remain; no independent garment region disappears.
Final F seated and crouched views retain coat separation from trousers/waistcoat; folds remain angular without the rejected inner-clothing islands.
Final CW/PW seated views have continuous coat surfaces without the previously rejected trouser islands.
Independent body swap retains casual headwear/gloves/low shoes on PW; removing CS footwear restores bare feet and the long trouser hem.
Mixed PS/formal-shoe and PW/tall-boot closeups show the selected trouser hem meeting the shoe/boot collar; no bare calf or full trouser tube crosses the boot.

All four presentation screenshots were inspected: the single figure and complete 8x8 cohorts are visible in the same room/camera, with the worn cohort cycling the 11 outfits. These distant, noninteractive scenes measure candidate rendering cost, not close-up visual acceptance or campaign performance.

All four final glove closeups were inspected directly because earlier glove-detail captures did not match pixel hashes. Each retains its own material on the relaxed hand; adjacent body regions remain exposed, with no production item grip claimed.

Prior native11 reuse is limited to inspected head/glove details; native12 reuse is limited to the bare body; native13 reuse is limited to the repaired bare-footwear details. Rejected garment/footwear intersections are never treated as passing reused review.
